edges.description: Loss of CoQ limits coupled electron transfer between respiratory complexes.
Oxidant accumulation varies with cell model and assay; a single mitochondrial ROS pattern is not established.
COQ6 knockdown reduces nephrin/F-actin and disrupts actin organization; intermediates are unresolved.
Knockdown-associated apoptosis is partly reversed by CoQ10 supplementation.
Genetic disease and rat expression support cochlear involvement, but the initiating cell lesion is unresolved.
Optic neuropathy is documented clinically; its cellular route from CoQ deficiency remains unresolved.
Impaired coupled respiration is associated with low cellular ATP in the same edited-cell model.
Loss of podocyte structural integrity provides a plausible route to impaired filtration; the cellular-to-organ link is inferred.
Podocyte depletion can impair filtration integrity; the human organ link extends the cell-culture findings.
Loss of filtration selectivity permits urinary protein loss.
Persistent podocyte injury can lead to segmental scarring; this is not the only reported biopsy pattern.
Persistent urinary protein loss can lower serum albumin.
Nephrotic protein loss and altered fluid handling can cause edema.
Glomerular injury can manifest as nephrotic syndrome; steroid resistance is determined clinically, not inferred from the mechanism.
Chronic renal injury can progress to kidney failure, with substantial variability and potential treatment benefit.
Cochlear dysfunction is a working explanation for sensorineural impairment; localization alone does not identify the causal cell type.
Optic nerve injury can leave persistent atrophy despite improvement in visual acuity.
